web_evidence.title: The Sum of All Fears — Prologue: Broken Arrow
web_evidence.note: The sustained excerpt hosted on Tom Clancy's official site externally narrates the 1973 combat setting and Israeli personnel in third person, with no participating narrator.

web_evidence.title: 20.15: Third Person Omniscient | Writing Excuses
web_evidence.note: The professional writing discussion explicitly identifies the Act III chapter Three Shakes as third-person omniscient narration and explains that its events cannot belong to any character's viewpoint.

web_evidence.title: Tom Clancy and Orientalism: Arabs and Muslims in the Contemporary Technothriller Novel
web_evidence.note: This University of Jyväskylä thesis analyzes the novel's numerous character-centered plot strands and reproduces third-person passages from both the opening and interior, including narration through Motti Zadin and Ghosn.

person_note: The controlling narrator is nonparticipating and narrates multiple characters and locations in third person, sometimes widening into omniscient technical exposition. The diagnostic Goodreads passages agree with the official third-person opening, the interior Three Shakes analysis, and the scholarly study's opening and interior examples. First- and second-person forms in the supplied quotes occur only in speech, aphorisms, or the Churchill epigraph, so they do not create alternating narration. The main limitation is that the authorized excerpt covers only the opening, but independently documented interior narration and whole-book structural analysis resolve that scope limitation.
